perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: Admin delete silently succeeded under RLS rejection —/api/admin/{courses,templates} DELETE(and coursesPUT) used the cookie-bound getSupabaseServerClient(). When RLS rejected the write, supabase returned { error: null, data: [] }— no error, zero rows affected — and the route returned 200 success. Frontend optimistically removed the row, success toast fired, but the row reappeared on refresh. User-visible symptom: "delete is not possible to the admin" (visible UI + invisible failure). Fix: switch the actual write togetSupabaseAdmin()(service-role) after the existingprofiles.role === 'admin'gate, plus assert non-empty.select('id') to convert silent zero-row writes into 404. Same pattern as 7 other admin routes (cardcom/refund, template-access, export, import, generate-cover, expenses, course-access). 6-case regression test (src/tests/admin-courses-delete-route.test.ts) explicitly guards the silent-success class. Violates the project rule "NO silent failures".

perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: Bulk-bar dropdowns opened LEFT in RTL + concurrent-403 on /admin/free-content — Two issues shipped together. (a) BulkActionsBar's <DropdownMenuContent align="end">flips to LEFT side of trigger in RTL (Radix semantics), making menus overflow off the bar; fixed withalign="start"+sideOffset={4}+collisionPadding={16}. (b) /admin/free-contentfired TWO concurrentfetch('/api/admin/courses?list=1')requests inPromise.all; under CF Workers + OpenNext, two parallel admin auth checks could race and one returned 403 ("Error: אין הרשאת מנהל"). Fix: merge into one combined fetch with productModes=[...COURSE,...LIVE].join(',')and partition response client-side byproduct_mode. Strictly safer regardless of root cause; halves admin-auth roundtrips on the page. Includes a 25-scenario e2e/admin-bulk-actions-dropdowns.spec.tscovering 5 pages × 5 dropdowns.

perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: Scroll up dead on agent terminals (Codex+Claude): root cause = mouse-report stole the wheel even on the PRIMARY screen, where the scrollback lives in our grid and the inline agent ignores wheel — so scroll-up black-holed. Fix: mouse-report owns the wheel only on the alternate screen; primary-screen wheel → our history. Regression: tests/terminal-mouse.spec.ts asserts primary-screen mouse-report wheel routes to history while alternate-screen mouse-report still sends VT mouse reports. Proof: npm run verify:terminal-mouse and npm run verify:map-terminals passed on 2026-06-24.

perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: Reliable map-terminal session binding + auto-resume: 100% of map terminal nodes must reattach to their correct persistent daemon session on open/startup, and auto-resume the agent (claude --resume <uuid> / codex resume <uuid>) when the session is a bare shell (agent exited), instead of spawning a NEW empty shell each open. Root cause observed 2026-07-13: opening a project makes a fresh terminal-<uuid>-<uuid> session (bare shell) rather than reattaching the live one, so resumes orphan and panes show dead shells. Session UUIDs are on disk (agent-fleet snapshot; claude ~/.claude/projects, codex ~/.codex/sessions). Investigation-first: map how map nodes bind to daemon sessions (frontend store + EnsureSession id scheme), then design deterministic node→session keying + auto-resume hook. See memory project_termfleet_daemon_wedge_recovery. Root cause found + fixed (2026-07-13): recovery is PER-PANE (terminal-<tabId>-<paneId>), not per-folder; each pane's conversation id lives in agent-status/pane-<fnv(paneId)>.json. Daemon cold-restore now (a) resumes claude via id-only fallback (mirrors codex) and (b) enriches a bare/hand-started session from its per-pane sidecar (read_pane_sidecar_recovery → plan_agent_restore), so every node restores ITS OWN chat on daemon recycle / reboot / shutdown. codex/claude status hooks stamp provider. Proof: 105 lib tests pass incl. 7 new (fnv parity vs real sidecar name, sidecar-recovery variants, hand-started cold-restore); npm run doctor TC-054 check green + reports 19/19 nodes recoverable; design in docs/tc-054-agent-autoresume-design.md. Pending: activates on next launcher restart (running daemon predates the build); full reboot E2E not yet run.

perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: Safe dead-process / session eradicator (reaper): periodically reap DEAD/closed sessions and their orphaned tool servers (dev servers, Playwright browsers, language servers, esbuild watchers, node_repl) that agents leave running after /exit. Must gate every kill on a DEEP agent-in-tree scan (a shallow direct-child check gave false positives on 2026-07-13 because agents nest under wrappers) plus an idle-CPU gate, so a live conversation is never killed. Ship dry-run first (log what it would kill), then arm on a timer. Motivated by the 2026-07-13 outage where ~3,500 accumulated processes starved RAM+swap and wedged the daemon. Dry-run shipped + tested (2026-07-13): scripts/termfleet-reaper.mjs with a pure reapDecision safety gate (deep agent-in-tree scan → never reap a session with a live agent anywhere in its tree; idle-window gate; skips sessions with nothing to reclaim). Run node scripts/termfleet-reaper.mjs (dry-run) / --apply / --idle=<sec>. Coverage fixed + soft load guardrail added (2026-07-13): reaper now enumerates sessions from the daemon's own listSessions (reuse termfleetctl.requestDaemon) instead of a cgroup session-leader guess that saw 2 of 15 sessions; the deep agent scan now INCLUDES the session root pid (agents often run as the root — the miss that mislabeled them bare shells); idle now comes from the per-pane sidecar updatedAt (reuse paneSidecarPath), not process start-age. Live dry-run covers all 15 sessions and keeps every live-agent one. Separately, the daemon's transient systemd unit (platform_process.rs) now sets a SOFT MemoryHigh (throttle+reclaim, NEVER OOM-kill) + high TasksMax fork-bomb backstop (env-overridable TERMFLEET_DAEMON_MEMORY_HIGH/_TASKS_MAX; no hard MemoryMax by design), so daemon load can't wedge the desktop and no agent is silently killed. npm run doctor reports daemon memory headroom + flags a daemon predating the guardrail. Proof: 8 reaper policy tests + 106 lib tests (incl. argv guardrail assertion). Now fully automatic (2026-07-14): scripts/install-reaper-timer.sh installs a systemd --user timer (mirrors agent-fleet-snapshot) that every 15 min runs a oneshot which (1) scripts/termfleet-guardrail-ensure.mjs applies the soft MemoryHigh/TasksMax to the running daemon LIVE via systemctl set-property (self-healing for a daemon predating the code; idempotent needsGuardrail gate, tested) and (2) termfleet-reaper.mjs --apply reaps idle leftovers. Guardrail default lowered 55G→40G (leaves desktop headroom). Verified live: guardrail applied to the running daemon (MemoryHigh infinity→40G, no restart, no killed agents), timer armed (systemctl --user list-timers), a triggered run kept all live-agent sessions + reaped 0, and npm run doctor shows guardrail ok (30.6/40G) + "reaper timer is armed". Note: timer install is per-machine via the script; the daemon MemoryHigh default in platform_process.rs covers fresh launches.

perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: The cockpit task line is always true, always current, always readable — the operator's four invariants: never blank (Task not captured must never render), never invented (every word is the agent's own, the operator's own, or a fixed template over a verified fact), never stale (the line dies when its turn ends), always plain (a non-developer can read it). Floor rule: when nothing better is knowable, show the operator's own request; for an agent-less shell, show what that terminal is actually doing. Root causes measured 2026-07-22: the Task row accepts only agent-declared text (present in 79/215 panes) while the templated activity string exists for 196/215 and is forbidden; quality-gate rejection renders the same string as "no data"; the 30-minute sidecar TTL lets finished tasks linger; shell panes have no derivation path; nothing reads the vendor session transcripts. New evidence: Claude and Codex both write hook-free on-disk session records (~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl incl. ai-title + last-prompt; ~/.codex/sessions//rollout-*.jsonl incl. task_started/task_complete), Claude keeps a pid-keyed live registry at ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, and the process table maps every pane to its conversation id — together covering 209/215 panes vs 79 today, with shells covered by the process route. Design: a single daemon-owned resolver with a six-rung provenance ladder, per-rung expiry driven by real turn boundaries, and npm run verify:task-line sweeping every live pane as the release gate. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-reliable-task-line-design.md; plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-reliable-task-line.md. Shipped 2026-07-22 (core): the app now reads both vendors' own session records, resolves a seven-rung ladder that cannot return blank, and threads it through the header view model into all three surfaces; Rust gained an allowlisted transcript tail-reader and a pane foreground-command reader. Proof: 6 cargo tests, 22 frontend tests, npm run verify:task-line sweeps all 17 live panes with zero violations (agent-said 6, session-title 4, operator-request 3, current-tool 2, declared 1, shell-state 1 — every one previously Task not captured), npm run verify:task-identity 17/17, npm run build and npm run doctor pass with both vendor drift probes green. Plumbing fix 2026-07-28 (operator report "tasks still don't appear", four screenshots): the ladder and the records were both fine — a replay of the real resolver over all 238 live status files plus the vendor records produced a real line for every one of them, while the cockpit showed No task declared on idle Claude panes, a running Codex pane, and a pane that was mid-question. Four pieces of plumbing lost it: (1) summarizeAgentStatus attached the line only to its no-endpoint return, so the endpoint and error paths dropped it; (2) statusPollLoop — the ONLY loop that visits panes whose runtime is off screen — computed the line and never applied it, and statusPollProjectionChanged could not see it anyway, so every card that was not the one on screen had no line at all; (3) persistedTerminalSnapshot dropped it, so the first paint after every relaunch started empty and the header's own factless re-resolve printed the placeholder; (4) MagicCanvas/SplitPane read only the terminal's line while agent-kind tabs store it on the workstream. Added on the operator's request: a pending-question rung that states what the agent is asking them (Waiting on your answer: how should the blur over the pixelation be controlled, from Claude's own AskUserQuestion record, dropped again as soon as a later tool call shows it was answered) and a recent-activity rung so the agent's own newest note beats admitting nothing is known. Proof: tests/task-line-live-records.spec.ts (new — drives the real summarizer with real readers for BOTH on-disk sources; 238/238 panes render a real line, and it fails if a readable record yields the placeholder), tests/task-line-plumbing.spec.ts (new — 10 checks pinning each hole above), 64/64 of the existing task-line/identity/poll/transcript/audit suites, npm run build, and npm run doctor reporting Task line coverage: 21/21. New probe: npm run cockpit:why. Readable goal 2026-07-28 (operator: "I need a user readable main goal... if I come a week from now I have no idea what this is about"): two live cards read exercise-demo-gif-pipeline and fix-cockpit-task-display. Verified origin: both are Claude's OWN session title for those conversations (no Codex record contains either), and the vendor rewrites that title as a session runs — the same exercise session earlier carried the readable "Find free exercise visualization tool for fitness bot" and the app took the newest. Meanwhile the best answer to "what is this about" was unread: the operator's opening request lives at the START of the record and the app only ever read the tail (which carries "/done", "go"). Now: Rust gained a head reader (session_transcript_head_read, 64 KiB, same allowlisted dirs and id validation as the tail); a new opening-request rung leads the ladder under declared; the clearest session title wins over the newest; a slug is spaced into words (Fix cockpit task display) and audit:panes fails on any slug-shaped Task row; the composer's ❯ glyph is stripped; and the card's Task row is a FIXED two-line box (the terminal-jiggle contract in tests/cockpit-row-stability.spec.ts was deliberately re-pinned from "one line" to "two lines at a fixed height" — the jiggle came from a row whose height varied with the text; the fleet list stays one line). Fitting now allows 150 characters with the 200-character paste ceiling unchanged. Proof: 49/49 verify:task-line, audit:panes green with the new no-slug rule, 149/151 across the header suites (one pre-existing failure from a concurrent session), 7/7 Rust tc060 tests including a new head-reader bound, and cockpit:why on the live records shows opening-request and de-slugged titles in place of the slugs. Remaining: delete the per-project hardcoded outcome strings, feed the foreground command into the running-command rung, and demote the top rungs from live turn-end events end to end.

Fix: mouse-report owns the wheel only on the alternate screen; primary-screen wheel → our history. Regression: tests/terminal-mouse.spec.ts asserts primary-screen mouse-report wheel routes to history while alternate-screen mouse-report still sends VT mouse reports. Proof: npm run verify:terminal-mouse and npm run verify:map-terminals passed on 2026-06-24.

perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: Severe terminal typing lag in the map: readable map workspaces were mounting too many live terminal renderers, detached grid feeds could stay subscribed while idle, terminal snapshot/header updates refreshed too often for typing, and permanent map layer promotion kept WebKitGTK busy on large terminal maps. Fix limits the live map renderer to the primary work surface, slows preview/header churn, makes grid feed detach/subscriber cleanup explicit, and removes always-on map transform promotion/entry animation. Proof: clean Tauri dev restart on the persisted 12-terminal map dropped WebKit from ~40-55% steady to ~5.5% with grid feed ~0.3%; npm run build, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test term_state_dirty, npm run verify:map-terminals, and npx playwright test tests/map-terminal-rendering.spec.ts -g "readable map mounts only the primary live terminal renderer" --reporter=line passed on 2026-06-25.

perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: Reliable map-terminal session binding + auto-resume: 100% of map terminal nodes must reattach to their correct persistent daemon session on open/startup, and auto-resume the agent (claude --resume <uuid> / codex resume <uuid>) when the session is a bare shell (agent exited), instead of spawning a NEW empty shell each open. Root cause observed 2026-07-13: opening a project makes a fresh terminal-<uuid>-<uuid> session (bare shell) rather than reattaching the live one, so resumes orphan and panes show dead shells. Session UUIDs are on disk (agent-fleet snapshot; claude ~/.claude/projects, codex ~/.codex/sessions). Investigation-first: map how map nodes bind to daemon sessions (frontend store + EnsureSession id scheme), then design deterministic node→session keying + auto-resume hook. See memory project_termfleet_daemon_wedge_recovery. Root cause found + fixed (2026-07-13): recovery is PER-PANE (terminal-<tabId>-<paneId>), not per-folder; each pane's conversation id lives in agent-status/pane-<fnv(paneId)>.json. Daemon cold-restore now (a) resumes claude via id-only fallback (mirrors codex) and (b) enriches a bare/hand-started session from its per-pane sidecar (read_pane_sidecar_recovery → plan_agent_restore), so every node restores ITS OWN chat on daemon recycle / reboot / shutdown. codex/claude status hooks stamp provider. Proof: 105 lib tests pass incl. 7 new (fnv parity vs real sidecar name, sidecar-recovery variants, hand-started cold-restore); npm run doctor TC-054 check green + reports 19/19 nodes recoverable; design in docs/tc-054-agent-autoresume-design.md. Pending: activates on next launcher restart (running daemon predates the build); full reboot E2E not yet run.

perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: Safe dead-process / session eradicator (reaper): periodically reap DEAD/closed sessions and their orphaned tool servers (dev servers, Playwright browsers, language servers, esbuild watchers, node_repl) that agents leave running after /exit. Must gate every kill on a DEEP agent-in-tree scan (a shallow direct-child check gave false positives on 2026-07-13 because agents nest under wrappers) plus an idle-CPU gate, so a live conversation is never killed. Ship dry-run first (log what it would kill), then arm on a timer. Motivated by the 2026-07-13 outage where ~3,500 accumulated processes starved RAM+swap and wedged the daemon. Dry-run shipped + tested (2026-07-13): scripts/termfleet-reaper.mjs with a pure reapDecision safety gate (deep agent-in-tree scan → never reap a session with a live agent anywhere in its tree; idle-window gate; skips sessions with nothing to reclaim). Run node scripts/termfleet-reaper.mjs (dry-run) / --apply / --idle=<sec>. Coverage fixed + soft load guardrail added (2026-07-13): reaper now enumerates sessions from the daemon's own listSessions (reuse termfleetctl.requestDaemon) instead of a cgroup session-leader guess that saw 2 of 15 sessions; the deep agent scan now INCLUDES the session root pid (agents often run as the root — the miss that mislabeled them bare shells); idle now comes from the per-pane sidecar updatedAt (reuse paneSidecarPath), not process start-age. Live dry-run covers all 15 sessions and keeps every live-agent one. Separately, the daemon's transient systemd unit (platform_process.rs) now sets a SOFT MemoryHigh (throttle+reclaim, NEVER OOM-kill) + high TasksMax fork-bomb backstop (env-overridable TERMFLEET_DAEMON_MEMORY_HIGH/_TASKS_MAX; no hard MemoryMax by design), so daemon load can't wedge the desktop and no agent is silently killed. npm run doctor reports daemon memory headroom + flags a daemon predating the guardrail. Proof: 8 reaper policy tests + 106 lib tests (incl. argv guardrail assertion). Now fully automatic (2026-07-14): scripts/install-reaper-timer.sh installs a systemd --user timer (mirrors agent-fleet-snapshot) that every 15 min runs a oneshot which (1) scripts/termfleet-guardrail-ensure.mjs applies the soft MemoryHigh/TasksMax to the running daemon LIVE via systemctl set-property (self-healing for a daemon predating the code; idempotent needsGuardrail gate, tested) and (2) termfleet-reaper.mjs --apply reaps idle leftovers. Guardrail default lowered 55G→40G (leaves desktop headroom). Verified live: guardrail applied to the running daemon (MemoryHigh infinity→40G, no restart, no killed agents), timer armed (systemctl --user list-timers), a triggered run kept all live-agent sessions + reaped 0, and npm run doctor shows guardrail ok (30.6/40G) + "reaper timer is armed". Note: timer install is per-machine via the script; the daemon MemoryHigh default in platform_process.rs covers fresh launches.

perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: The cockpit task line is always true, always current, always readable — the operator's four invariants: never blank (Task not captured must never render), never invented (every word is the agent's own, the operator's own, or a fixed template over a verified fact), never stale (the line dies when its turn ends), always plain (a non-developer can read it). Floor rule: when nothing better is knowable, show the operator's own request; for an agent-less shell, show what that terminal is actually doing. Root causes measured 2026-07-22: the Task row accepts only agent-declared text (present in 79/215 panes) while the templated activity string exists for 196/215 and is forbidden; quality-gate rejection renders the same string as "no data"; the 30-minute sidecar TTL lets finished tasks linger; shell panes have no derivation path; nothing reads the vendor session transcripts. New evidence: Claude and Codex both write hook-free on-disk session records (~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl incl. ai-title + last-prompt; ~/.codex/sessions//rollout-*.jsonl incl. task_started/task_complete), Claude keeps a pid-keyed live registry at ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, and the process table maps every pane to its conversation id — together covering 209/215 panes vs 79 today, with shells covered by the process route. Design: a single daemon-owned resolver with a six-rung provenance ladder, per-rung expiry driven by real turn boundaries, and npm run verify:task-line sweeping every live pane as the release gate. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-reliable-task-line-design.md; plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-reliable-task-line.md. Shipped 2026-07-22 (core): the app now reads both vendors' own session records, resolves a seven-rung ladder that cannot return blank, and threads it through the header view model into all three surfaces; Rust gained an allowlisted transcript tail-reader and a pane foreground-command reader. Proof: 6 cargo tests, 22 frontend tests, npm run verify:task-line sweeps all 17 live panes with zero violations (agent-said 6, session-title 4, operator-request 3, current-tool 2, declared 1, shell-state 1 — every one previously Task not captured), npm run verify:task-identity 17/17, npm run build and npm run doctor pass with both vendor drift probes green. Plumbing fix 2026-07-28 (operator report "tasks still don't appear", four screenshots): the ladder and the records were both fine — a replay of the real resolver over all 238 live status files plus the vendor records produced a real line for every one of them, while the cockpit showed No task declared on idle Claude panes, a running Codex pane, and a pane that was mid-question. Four pieces of plumbing lost it: (1) summarizeAgentStatus attached the line only to its no-endpoint return, so the endpoint and error paths dropped it; (2) statusPollLoop — the ONLY loop that visits panes whose runtime is off screen — computed the line and never applied it, and statusPollProjectionChanged could not see it anyway, so every card that was not the one on screen had no line at all; (3) persistedTerminalSnapshot dropped it, so the first paint after every relaunch started empty and the header's own factless re-resolve printed the placeholder; (4) MagicCanvas/SplitPane read only the terminal's line while agent-kind tabs store it on the workstream. Added on the operator's request: a pending-question rung that states what the agent is asking them (Waiting on your answer: how should the blur over the pixelation be controlled, from Claude's own AskUserQuestion record, dropped again as soon as a later tool call shows it was answered) and a recent-activity rung so the agent's own newest note beats admitting nothing is known. Proof: tests/task-line-live-records.spec.ts (new — drives the real summarizer with real readers for BOTH on-disk sources; 238/238 panes render a real line, and it fails if a readable record yields the placeholder), tests/task-line-plumbing.spec.ts (new — 10 checks pinning each hole above), 64/64 of the existing task-line/identity/poll/transcript/audit suites, npm run build, and npm run doctor reporting Task line coverage: 21/21. New probe: npm run cockpit:why. Readable goal 2026-07-28 (operator: "I need a user readable main goal... if I come a week from now I have no idea what this is about"): two live cards read exercise-demo-gif-pipeline and fix-cockpit-task-display. Verified origin: both are Claude's OWN session title for those conversations (no Codex record contains either), and the vendor rewrites that title as a session runs — the same exercise session earlier carried the readable "Find free exercise visualization tool for fitness bot" and the app took the newest. Meanwhile the best answer to "what is this about" was unread: the operator's opening request lives at the START of the record and the app only ever read the tail (which carries "/done", "go"). Now: Rust gained a head reader (session_transcript_head_read, 64 KiB, same allowlisted dirs and id validation as the tail); a new opening-request rung leads the ladder under declared; the clearest session title wins over the newest; a slug is spaced into words (Fix cockpit task display) and audit:panes fails on any slug-shaped Task row; the composer's ❯ glyph is stripped; and the card's Task row is a FIXED two-line box (the terminal-jiggle contract in tests/cockpit-row-stability.spec.ts was deliberately re-pinned from "one line" to "two lines at a fixed height" — the jiggle came from a row whose height varied with the text; the fleet list stays one line). Fitting now allows 150 characters with the 200-character paste ceiling unchanged. Proof: 49/49 verify:task-line, audit:panes green with the new no-slug rule, 149/151 across the header suites (one pre-existing failure from a concurrent session), 7/7 Rust tc060 tests including a new head-reader bound, and cockpit:why on the live records shows opening-request and de-slugged titles in place of the slugs. Remaining: delete the per-project hardcoded outcome strings, feed the foreground command into the running-command rung, and demote the top rungs from live turn-end events end to end.

Fix: mouse-report owns the wheel only on the alternate screen; primary-screen wheel → our history. Regression: tests/terminal-mouse.spec.ts asserts primary-screen mouse-report wheel routes to history while alternate-screen mouse-report still sends VT mouse reports. Proof: npm run verify:terminal-mouse and npm run verify:map-terminals passed on 2026-06-24.

perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: Safe dead-process / session eradicator (reaper): periodically reap DEAD/closed sessions and their orphaned tool servers (dev servers, Playwright browsers, language servers, esbuild watchers, node_repl) that agents leave running after /exit. Must gate every kill on a DEEP agent-in-tree scan (a shallow direct-child check gave false positives on 2026-07-13 because agents nest under wrappers) plus an idle-CPU gate, so a live conversation is never killed. Ship dry-run first (log what it would kill), then arm on a timer. Motivated by the 2026-07-13 outage where ~3,500 accumulated processes starved RAM+swap and wedged the daemon. Dry-run shipped + tested (2026-07-13): scripts/termfleet-reaper.mjs with a pure reapDecision safety gate (deep agent-in-tree scan → never reap a session with a live agent anywhere in its tree; idle-window gate; skips sessions with nothing to reclaim). Run node scripts/termfleet-reaper.mjs (dry-run) / --apply / --idle=<sec>. Coverage fixed + soft load guardrail added (2026-07-13): reaper now enumerates sessions from the daemon's own listSessions (reuse termfleetctl.requestDaemon) instead of a cgroup session-leader guess that saw 2 of 15 sessions; the deep agent scan now INCLUDES the session root pid (agents often run as the root — the miss that mislabeled them bare shells); idle now comes from the per-pane sidecar updatedAt (reuse paneSidecarPath), not process start-age. Live dry-run covers all 15 sessions and keeps every live-agent one. Separately, the daemon's transient systemd unit (platform_process.rs) now sets a SOFT MemoryHigh (throttle+reclaim, NEVER OOM-kill) + high TasksMax fork-bomb backstop (env-overridable TERMFLEET_DAEMON_MEMORY_HIGH/_TASKS_MAX; no hard MemoryMax by design), so daemon load can't wedge the desktop and no agent is silently killed. npm run doctor reports daemon memory headroom + flags a daemon predating the guardrail. Proof: 8 reaper policy tests + 106 lib tests (incl. argv guardrail assertion). perOriginalRowReconciliation.originalTitle: The cockpit task line is always true, always current, always readable — the operator's four invariants: never blank (Task not captured must never render), never invented (every word is the agent's own, the operator's own, or a fixed template over a verified fact), never stale (the line dies when its turn ends), always plain (a non-developer can read it). Floor rule: when nothing better is knowable, show the operator's own request; for an agent-less shell, show what that terminal is actually doing. Root causes measured 2026-07-22: the Task row accepts only agent-declared text (present in 79/215 panes) while the templated activity string exists for 196/215 and is forbidden; quality-gate rejection renders the same string as "no data"; the 30-minute sidecar TTL lets finished tasks linger; shell panes have no derivation path; nothing reads the vendor session transcripts. New evidence: Claude and Codex both write hook-free on-disk session records (~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl incl. ai-title + last-prompt; ~/.codex/sessions//rollout-*.jsonl incl. task_started/task_complete), Claude keeps a pid-keyed live registry at ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, and the process table maps every pane to its conversation id — together covering 209/215 panes vs 79 today, with shells covered by the process route. Design: a single daemon-owned resolver with a six-rung provenance ladder, per-rung expiry driven by real turn boundaries, and npm run verify:task-line sweeping every live pane as the release gate. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-reliable-task-line-design.md; plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-reliable-task-line.md. Shipped 2026-07-22 (core): the app now reads both vendors' own session records, resolves a seven-rung ladder that cannot return blank, and threads it through the header view model into all three surfaces; Rust gained an allowlisted transcript tail-reader and a pane foreground-command reader. Proof: 6 cargo tests, 22 frontend tests, npm run verify:task-line sweeps all 17 live panes with zero violations (agent-said 6, session-title 4, operator-request 3, current-tool 2, declared 1, shell-state 1 — every one previously Task not captured), npm run verify:task-identity 17/17, npm run build and npm run doctor pass with both vendor drift probes green. Plumbing fix 2026-07-28 (operator report "tasks still don't appear", four screenshots): the ladder and the records were both fine — a replay of the real resolver over all 238 live status files plus the vendor records produced a real line for every one of them, while the cockpit showed No task declared on idle Claude panes, a running Codex pane, and a pane that was mid-question. Four pieces of plumbing lost it: (1) summarizeAgentStatus attached the line only to its no-endpoint return, so the endpoint and error paths dropped it; (2) statusPollLoop — the ONLY loop that visits panes whose runtime is off screen — computed the line and never applied it, and statusPollProjectionChanged could not see it anyway, so every card that was not the one on screen had no line at all; (3) persistedTerminalSnapshot dropped it, so the first paint after every relaunch started empty and the header's own factless re-resolve printed the placeholder; (4) MagicCanvas/SplitPane read only the terminal's line while agent-kind tabs store it on the workstream. Added on the operator's request: a pending-question rung that states what the agent is asking them (Waiting on your answer: how should the blur over the pixelation be controlled, from Claude's own AskUserQuestion record, dropped again as soon as a later tool call shows it was answered) and a recent-activity rung so the agent's own newest note beats admitting nothing is known. Proof: tests/task-line-live-records.spec.ts (new — drives the real summarizer with real readers for BOTH on-disk sources; 238/238 panes render a real line, and it fails if a readable record yields the placeholder), tests/task-line-plumbing.spec.ts (new — 10 checks pinning each hole above), 64/64 of the existing task-line/identity/poll/transcript/audit suites, npm run build, and npm run doctor reporting Task line coverage: 21/21. New probe: npm run cockpit:why. Readable goal 2026-07-28 (operator: "I need a user readable main goal... if I come a week from now I have no idea what this is about"): two live cards read exercise-demo-gif-pipeline and fix-cockpit-task-display. Verified origin: both are Claude's OWN session title for those conversations (no Codex record contains either), and the vendor rewrites that title as a session runs — the same exercise session earlier carried the readable "Find free exercise visualization tool for fitness bot" and the app took the newest. Meanwhile the best answer to "what is this about" was unread: the operator's opening request lives at the START of the record and the app only ever read the tail (which carries "/done", "go"). Now: Rust gained a head reader (session_transcript_head_read, 64 KiB, same allowlisted dirs and id validation as the tail); a new opening-request rung leads the ladder under declared; the clearest session title wins over the newest; a slug is spaced into words (Fix cockpit task display) and audit:panes fails on any slug-shaped Task row; the composer's ❯ glyph is stripped; and the card's Task row is a FIXED two-line box (the terminal-jiggle contract in tests/cockpit-row-stability.spec.ts was deliberately re-pinned from "one line" to "two lines at a fixed height" — the jiggle came from a row whose height varied with the text; the fleet list stays one line). Fitting now allows 150 characters with the 200-character paste ceiling unchanged. Proof: 49/49 verify:task-line, audit:panes green with the new no-slug rule, 149/151 across the header suites (one pre-existing failure from a concurrent session), 7/7 Rust tc060 tests including a new head-reader bound, and cockpit:why on the live records shows opening-request and de-slugged titles in place of the slugs. Remaining: delete the per-project hardcoded outcome strings, feed the foreground command into the running-command rung, and demote the top rungs from live turn-end events end to end.
